title: Strings
bridge: Strings in Java are objects with methods: `s.length()`, `s.charAt(0)`, `s.substring(1, 4)`, `s.toUpperCase()`, `s.trim()`, `s.split(",")`. The big trap: **compare text with `.equals()`**, never `==` (which checks if they're the same object, not the same letters).
lesson:
A `String` is text, and it comes with methods:

- `s.length()`: how many characters
- `s.charAt(0)`: the first character (a `char`); positions start at 0
- `s.substring(0, 4)`: from 0 up to (not including) 4; `s.substring(4)` from 4 to the end
- `s.toUpperCase()`, `s.toLowerCase()`, `s.trim()` (remove spaces at the ends)
- `s.contains("ma")`, `s.startsWith("07")`, `s.indexOf("a")` (-1 if missing)
- `s.replace("a", "b")`, `s.split(",")` (gives a `String[]` array)
- `String.join(", ", parts)` glues an array back together

Strings never change: methods give a **new** string. `name.trim();` alone does nothing you keep; write `name = name.trim();`.

**The trap:** to compare text, use `a.equals(b)` (or `a.equalsIgnoreCase(b)`). `a == b` asks "are these the very same object in memory?", which is sometimes true and sometimes not for the same letters. It's one of the most famous Java bugs.

Building text in a loop? `StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); sb.append("x"); sb.toString();` is much faster than `+=` many times.

notes: trim, then capitalise the first letter.
== false, equals true: always use equals.
split into an array, join back.

exercises.title: Capitalise
exercises.prompt: Write capitalise(String s): trim it, then first letter upper case and the rest lower case. capitalise("  wANJIRU ") is "Wanjiru". An empty or all-spaces string gives "".

tests.hint_if_fail: substring(0, 1) of an empty string crashes: check isEmpty() after trimming.

exercises.title: Same word?
exercises.prompt: Write sameWord(String a, String b): true if they're the same word ignoring capitals and spaces at the ends. Use equals, not ==.

exercises.title: Initials
exercises.prompt: Write initials(String fullName): "Amina Wanjiru Odhiambo" gives "A.W.O." Extra spaces between words must not break it.

tests.hint_if_fail: Split on one or more spaces: trim().split("\\s+")
